title: A self-maintaining system can be read as inferring

statements.text: A system that keeps itself within a bounded set of states can be described as if its internal states infer the causes of its sensory states. The description does not say the system computes anything explicitly.

sources.quote: Therefore, the internal states (and their blanket) will appear to engage in active Bayesian inference.
they will appear to model—and act on—their world to preserve their functional and structural integrity, leading to homoeostasis and a simple form of autopoiesis.

Mathematically, this implies the existence of a Lyapunov function that turns out to be model evidence (i.e., self-evidence) in Bayesian statistics or surprise (i.e., self-information) in information theory.
variational free energy is a Lyapunov function for neuronal dynamics, which therefore conform to Hamilton’s principle of least action.
Put simply, it means that the internal states of a particular partition can be cast as encoding conditional or posterior Bayesian beliefs about external states.
Quantum fields, black holes, and other spatially-distributed or topologically-defined systems can, therefore, be regarded as Bayesian observers
by making agency a generic expectation, it makes the “merely physical” the special case demanding explanation
